categoryName: Baby care — diapers, wipes, infant formula, baby food, baby soap/oil/lotion, feeding bottles, rash cream

skuLines.line: Diaper pants — mass brand, small retail pack
skuLines.examples: MamyPoko Pants Extra Absorb S/M 9-16s; Pampers All Round Protection Pants S 10s; Huggies Wonder Pants M 8s; Teddyy Easy S 12s
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; spikes Jul-Sep monsoon when cloth nappies will not dry on a hill
skuLines.notes: The velocity SKU — small packs turn 3-4x faster than jumbo in a tiny catchment and keep cash free. Diapers are the worst freight-to-value ratio in the whole store (bulky, light, low margin), so plan a full pallet only against confirmed demand. GST cut to 5% in the Sept-2025 rationalisation, verify current rate on the invoice.

skuLines.line: Diaper pants — mass brand, value/jumbo pack
skuLines.examples: MamyPoko Pants Extra Absorb M 46s/L 42s; Huggies Complete Comfort Wonder Pants L 38s; Pampers All Round Protection Pants M 44s
skuLines.notes: Best rupees-per-cubic-foot of freight in the diaper block. Stock one jumbo per fast size (M, L) as the family restock pack; deeper than that dies on the shelf in a catchment of only ~100-250 infants.

skuLines.line: Diaper pants — monthly / mega monthly pack
skuLines.examples: Pampers Premium Care Pants M 104s; MamyPoko Pants Skin Breathe Care L 104s; Babyhug Advanced M 152s
skuLines.notes: Verified per-diaper cost on FirstCry runs ₹6.31 (economy newborn) to ₹30.90 (premium XXL). Carry exactly ONE monthly pack per popular size as an insurance SKU for the family that cannot drive 30-50 km to town — do not build a wall of them. High cash-per-unit, slow turn.

skuLines.examples: Pampers Premium Care Pants; Huggies Natural Soft Premium; Bambo Nature; Millette/Allter bamboo
skuLines.notes: Premium diapers are 658 of FirstCry's 1,637 diaper SKUs — the premiumisation is real but the buyer base here is a salaried teaching/admin household, so 1-2 premium options is the honest depth. Sells on 'no marks' and rash-free claims, not on price.

skuLines.examples: Teddyy Easy; Wowper Fresh; Little Angel; Niine Baby; Himalaya Total Care Baby Pants
skuLines.notes: The margin engine of the diaper block and the line that stops a price-sensitive household from stockpiling on a town trip. Himalaya baby pants start at ₹92 (verified on himalayawellness.in). Keep one regional/economy brand beside every MNC facing.

skuLines.examples: Pampers New Baby Taped NB; Huggies Taped Newborn; Babyhug taped NB; MamyPoko Standard NB
skuLines.notes: Taped is only 285 of 1,637 diaper SKUs nationally but it is non-substitutable for the first 6-10 weeks — a pant cannot be put on a newborn with an unhealed cord stump. In a closed township with staff deliveries happening every month, running out of NB taped is the classic wallet-leak event.

skuLines.examples: Pampers Premium Care Pants XXL 90s; MamyPoko Pants XXL 68s; Babyoye Air Soft XXL 30s
skuLines.notes: Only 144 XXL + 22 XXXL SKUs exist nationally, so supply is thin and substitution is poor. One facing per brand is enough, but it must never be zero: the 2-3 year old in a staff quarter has no fallback.

skuLines.line: Night pull-up pants for bedwetting (4-10 yrs)
skuLines.examples: MamyPoko/Pampers XXXL pants used off-label; Friends Easy pull-ups youth size; Dry Direct Slip small
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks in the cold months when children hold less
skuLines.notes: The quietly important line for a residential school taking children from age 5 — nocturnal enuresis runs ~15% at 5 and ~5% at 10. The buyer is a hostel matron or warden on an indent, not the child, so sell it as a discreet bulk line and keep it off the open aisle. Pair with bed protectors and baby laundry liquid.

skuLines.examples: Babyhug muslin square nappies; Mee Mee cotton nappy pack; local hosiery langot pack of 12
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; buy-in before winter when drying is slow
skuLines.notes: Highest-margin, lowest-freight-risk line in the category and the default in a hill household that cannot restock disposables weekly. Verified ₹199-₹349 for packs of 10-12 on Amazon. Caveat to state honestly at the counter: at 173101 monsoon humidity, cloth needs 2x the stock because nothing dries.

skuLines.examples: SuperBottoms UNO; Bumtum Freesize; Bummy Pants; Allter cloth diaper
skuLines.packSizes: Single or 3-pack, freesize 5-17 kg; insert packs of 3-6
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; avoid pushing in peak monsoon
skuLines.notes: Non-disposables are the fastest-growing diaper sub-segment in India (~7.8% CAGR) and 4,019 cloth SKUs now exist on FirstCry. Genuinely rational here: water and labour are available on campus, freight is one-off, and the household saves ₹800-₹1,500/month. Stock 2 SKUs, not 10 — it is a considered purchase, not a repeat.

skuLines.examples: Babyhug waterproof nappy pants; Mee Mee plastic pants; 1st Step PVC nappy cover
skuLines.seasonality: Peaks Jul-Sep monsoon and Nov-Feb winter
skuLines.notes: Cheap, tiny, never expires — the perfect hill SKU. Sells only as an attachment to cloth nappies, so shelve it directly beside them.

skuLines.examples: Babyhug quick-dry bed protector; Mee Mee rubber sheet; Newnik waterproof sheet
skuLines.notes: Serves two buyers at once: staff families with babies, and the hostel for bedwetting. Bulky but light and unbreakable — good freight fill for a diaper consignment. Zero expiry risk.

skuLines.examples: Babyhug disposable changing mats; Chicco changing mats
skuLines.notes: Genuinely optional in a closed township where nobody travels far. One facing at most.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Gentle Baby Wipes 72s; Pampers Fresh Clean 72s; Johnson's Baby Skincare Wipes 80s; Babyhug Premium 80s
skuLines.notes: Himalaya gentle baby wipes verified from ₹48 (himalayawellness.in). Watch the seal: a wipes pack whose flip-cap gasket fails dries out on the shelf and is a total write-off, so first-in-first-out matters more here than anywhere else in the category. Do NOT store near a leaky monsoon wall — the pack must stay sealed, not wet.

skuLines.line: Baby wet wipes — 99% water / unscented / paraben-free
skuLines.examples: Mother Sparsh 98% Water Wipes; Babyhug Advanced 99% Pure Water Unscented; Mamaearth Bamboo Wipes; Himalaya Shishu Anand
skuLines.notes: Unscented has grown to 288 SKUs vs 375 scented nationally and 99%-water claims now cover 210 SKUs — this is where the category is heading. Better margin than mass wipes and the line an educated teaching household actually asks for by name.

skuLines.line: Travel wipes, cotton wool roll and cotton balls
skuLines.examples: Johnson's travel wipes 10s/20s; Ruby/Bella cotton roll 100-500g; Babyhug cotton balls
skuLines.packSizes: Wipes 10-30 pcs; cotton roll 100g/300g/500g; cotton balls 100s
skuLines.notes: Cotton wool is the cheapest complete substitute for wipes and the fallback when a wipes consignment is stuck on a blocked hill road. Indefinite shelf life if kept dry. Also crosses over to the campus infirmary.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Diaper Rash Cream 20g/50g; Babyhug Advanced Rash Cream; Mee Mee Rash Cream; Chicco Nappy Cream
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp peak Jul-Sep monsoon; secondary peak in winter when nappies stay damp
skuLines.notes: THE emergency SKU of this whole category. Himalaya rash cream verified from ₹84. A crying baby with a raw bottom at 10pm and a 30-50 km road is exactly the failure this store exists to prevent — never let this go to zero, ever, in any season. Long shelf life (24-36 months), tiny, light, high turn. Only 89 rash-cream SKUs exist nationally, so substitution is limited.

skuLines.examples: Sudocrem Antiseptic Healing Cream 60g/125g; Sebamed Baby Rash Cream; Bepanthen Nappy Care; Desitin
skuLines.notes: Verified Sudocrem 60g ₹444-₹499, Sebamed rash cream ₹510-₹630. This is the step-up when the mass cream fails after 3 days, and the campus doctor will name it. Check the pack: some allopathic barrier creams are drug-scheduled and want a pharmacy licence — confirm each brand's classification before listing, and prefer the cosmetic/ayurvedic-registered ones if ARY has no drug licence.

skuLines.examples: Vaseline Baby Gentle Protective Jelly; Himalaya baby cream as barrier; Boroline (adult crossover)
skuLines.seasonality: Strong Nov-Feb winter peak — chapped cheeks, lips, nose
skuLines.notes: Verified Vaseline Blue Seal 50ml ₹225 tier. Crosses over hard to students, staff and the elderly in a cold hill winter, which is why it earns its shelf slot on total turns rather than baby turns alone. Never expires in practice.

skuLines.examples: Nestle NAN PRO 1; Nestle Lactogen 1; Aptamil Gold Stage 1; Similac Plus Stage 1 with 5-HMOs; Dexolac Stage 1
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round — the single least seasonal SKU in the store
skuLines.marginBand: 4-10% — the thinnest margin on the shelf
skuLines.notes: Verified: Lactogen 1 400g ₹310-₹330, Aptamil Gold Stage 1 400g ₹1,010, Similac Plus and NAN PRO in between. LICENCE + LAW: needs FSSAI, and the IMS Act 1992 (amended 2003) bans advertising, special display, discounts, coupons, free samples and tie-in sales on infant milk substitutes — sell at label price with no promotion and no shelf-talker. Store dry and raised: monsoon humidity at 173101 cakes an opened tin. Carry it as a trust line, not a profit line.

skuLines.examples: Nestle NAN PRO 2; Lactogen 2; Aptamil Gold+ Stage 2; Similac Advance Stage 2; Dexolac Stage 2
skuLines.notes: Verified NAN PRO Stage 2 ₹775, Dexolac Stage 2 400g ₹490, Similac Advance Stage 2 400g/800g. Same IMS Act restrictions apply. In a closed community you can actually forecast this: log each infant's birth month once and Stage 2 lands before Stage 1 runs out — nobody in open retail can do that.

skuLines.examples: Nestle NAN PRO 3 and 4; Aptamil Gold+ Stage 3; Lactogen 3; Nusobee 3
skuLines.notes: Stage 3/4 is where buffalo/cow milk starts substituting, so demand is softer and more price-elastic than Stage 1/2 — one brand deep is enough. Outside the IMS Act's under-2 promotion ban for Stage 4 in most readings, but treat the whole formula block as non-promotable to stay clean.

skuLines.examples: Dexolac; Lactodex; Nusobee; Amul Infant Milk Formula
skuLines.notes: Non-negotiable presence. A non-teaching-staff household on a hill salary buying Aptamil at ₹1,010 is not a real scenario; Dexolac at ₹490 is. Two price rungs (₹300-500 and ₹800-1,100) covers the whole campus.

skuLines.examples: Aptamil Gold Stage 1 1.2kg; Dexolac Stage 1 1.2kg; NAN PRO large bag-in-box
skuLines.notes: The hill-logistics answer — one purchase covers a month and cuts the household's trip risk. But it is the highest cash-per-unit item in the whole baby aisle on the thinnest margin, so stock to a named standing order only, never speculatively. Humidity risk is worse in a bag-in-box than a tin.

skuLines.examples: Isomil (soy); Lactogen LF; Similac Special Care / Similac Total Comfort; Neocate; Nusobee Soya
skuLines.notes: Only 1-6 SKUs exist per specialty brand nationally, so it is genuinely hard to source. Justified here only because there is no pharmacy within 30-50 km: a lactose-intolerant or preterm infant on this campus has no alternative supply at all. Stock against a doctor's named prescription, on indent, not on the open shelf. Confirm expiry on receipt — these move slowly.

skuLines.line: Milk cereal (with milk), 300g — by flavour and stage
skuLines.examples: Nestle Cerelac Wheat Apple 6m+; Cerelac Wheat Honey 8m+; Cerelac Ragi 6m+; Cerelac Khichdi Vegetables & Ghee 8m+; Cerelac 5 Grains & Fruits 18m+
skuLines.notes: Verified ₹260-₹300 for 300g on Amazon. The highest-velocity baby FOOD line in Indian general trade. Do not carry 15 flavours — carry the 4 the campus actually buys (Wheat Apple 6m+, Ragi 6m+, Wheat Honey 8m+, Multigrain & Fruits 12m+) and let the rest go. Opened box has ~3 weeks of use; unopened shelf life 12-18 months. Under the IMS Act 'infant foods' for under-2s are also non-promotable.

skuLines.examples: Nestle Nestum Rice 6-24m; Nestum Rice & Fruits 10-24m; Nestum Multigrain
skuLines.notes: Verified Nestum 300g pack-of-2 ₹350 (₹175/unit). The right answer for a mother mixing with her own breast milk or with fresh buffalo milk — which on a Himachal campus with local dairy is common. One or two variants.

skuLines.line: Traditional / organic weaning porridge — ragi, millet, sathu maavu
skuLines.examples: Timios Organic Sprouted Ragi Porridge; Timios Sattu Maavu; Slurrp Farm Sprouted Ragi; ByGrandma Sathu Maavu; Little Moppet Foods; Tummy Friendly Foods
skuLines.notes: The fastest-growing shape in Indian baby food and the best margin in this block: 375 porridge/cereal SKUs nationally, with Ragi 99, Multigrain 116, Sathu Maavu 29 SKUs. Fits a Sikh institutional household's preference for traditional grain over branded Western cereal, and fits the no-refined-sugar demand. Shorter shelf life than Cerelac (9-12 months) — order shallow and often.

skuLines.line: Growing-up cereal 2yr+ and nutrition add-on powders
skuLines.examples: Nestle Ceregrow Multigrain 300g; dry fruit powder; banana powder; sprouted ragi powder; Bonnisan/Dabur nutrition mixes
skuLines.notes: 41 add-on powder SKUs and 38 dry-fruit-powder SKUs exist nationally. Bridges baby care into the 2-6 year old cohort, which on this campus is large (pre-primary Academy children). Two SKUs maximum.

skuLines.line: Fruit and vegetable puree — pouch or jar, 100g
skuLines.examples: Happa Organic purees; Gerber jars; Ella's Kitchen pouches; Organix; Hipp
skuLines.packSizes: 100g pouch or 125g jar; often sold in 2s
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; more useful in monsoon when fresh fruit supply to the hill is erratic
skuLines.notes: Ready-to-feed is India's fastest-growing baby food format (~8% CAGR), 56 puree SKUs nationally. Ambient, no cold chain — but shelf life is only 12-18 months and velocity here will be low, so this is the single highest expiry-write-off risk in the category. Cap it at 2-3 SKUs, 6 units each, and reorder on sale not on schedule. Honest note: a campus with a fruit-and-veg counter can make fresh mashed banana for free, so sell this on convenience, not nutrition.

skuLines.line: Baby finger snacks — puffs, melties, teething sticks
skuLines.examples: Timios puffs; Slurrp Farm millet puffs; Gerber Puffs; NumNum melties; Happa teething sticks
skuLines.notes: 64 finger-food SKUs nationally. Good margin, tiny footprint, but 6-9 month shelf life and it goes soft fast in monsoon humidity — the pouch must stay sealed and off a damp wall. Two SKUs.

skuLines.examples: Timios Zookers animal-shaped biscuits; Slurrp Farm ragi cookies; Early Foods millet cookies
skuLines.notes: Verified Timios Zookers ₹142. The impulse SKU of the baby aisle and the one an older sibling drags a parent back for — put it at eye level of a 4-year-old. Also crosses over to the pre-primary Academy children. Short shelf life (6-9 months), so shallow and frequent.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Gentle Baby Soap 75g; Himalaya Extra Moisturizing Baby Soap; Johnson's Baby Soap 100g; Pears Baby; Dove Baby Bar
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; the moisturising variants peak Nov-Feb
skuLines.notes: Verified Himalaya Gentle Baby Soap from ₹45, Extra Moisturizing ₹65, Nourishing ₹65, Refreshing ₹62; Johnson's 100g ~₹64 single. Real crossover: baby soap is bought by adults on this kind of campus for dry winter skin, so it turns faster than the infant count suggests. Push multipacks — they cut per-unit freight and lock in a month.

skuLines.line: Baby body wash / head-to-toe liquid wash
skuLines.examples: Himalaya Gentle Baby Wash 200/400ml; Mamaearth Milky Soft Head to Toe Wash 400ml; Johnson's Top-to-Toe Wash; Cetaphil Baby Wash & Shampoo; Sebamed Baby Wash
skuLines.seasonality: Winter peak — liquid wash displaces soap when skin is dry
skuLines.notes: Verified Himalaya Gentle Baby Wash from ₹125, Extra Moisturizing from ₹115, Mamaearth Milky Soft 400ml ₹399, Cetaphil ₹1,169. Three rungs — Himalaya ₹115-₹160, Mamaearth ₹374-₹399, Cetaphil/Sebamed ₹1,000+ — covers the whole income spread on campus. Bottles are heavy: co-load with light diaper freight.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Gentle Baby Shampoo 100/200/400ml; Johnson's Baby Shampoo; Mamaearth Tear-Free Shampoo; Aveeno Baby Wash & Shampoo
skuLines.notes: Verified Himalaya Gentle Baby Shampoo from ₹106, Aveeno 532ml ₹944. Also bought for pre-primary children well past infancy, so the 400ml is the real hero pack here, not the 100ml.

skuLines.line: Baby massage oil — ayurvedic / lal tail
skuLines.examples: Dabur Lal Tail 50/100/200/500ml; Himalaya Baby Massage Oil; Johnson's Baby Oil; Bajaj Almond Drops (crossover)
skuLines.seasonality: Strong Nov-Feb winter peak — daily oil massage is standard in a cold North Indian household
skuLines.notes: Verified Dabur Lal Tail: 50ml ₹52, 100ml ₹110, 200ml ₹232, 500ml ₹419; Himalaya baby massage oil from ₹75. The most culturally non-negotiable line after diapers and rash cream in a North Indian setting. Glass/PET bottles — pack cushioned for hill road transit. Long shelf life (24-36 months).

skuLines.line: Baby hair oil and plain carrier oils
skuLines.examples: Himalaya Baby Hair Oil; Mamaearth Nourishing Hair Oil for Babies; cold-pressed coconut / almond / olive oil small packs
skuLines.notes: Verified Himalaya Baby Hair Oil from ₹151. Distinct buying occasion from massage oil (scalp, not body) and Indian mothers do not substitute. Note: JIVO already sells edible oils — do not let a cooking-oil facing satisfy this need, the buyer wants the baby label.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Baby Lotion 100/200/400ml; Himalaya Extra Moisturizing Baby Lotion; Mother Sparsh Milky Soft Lotion; Mamaearth Milky Soft Body Lotion 400ml; Sebamed Baby Lotion
skuLines.seasonality: Strong Nov-Feb winter peak; secondary post-bath use year-round
skuLines.notes: Verified Himalaya baby lotion from ₹115, Extra Moisturizing from ₹160, Mother Sparsh ₹198-₹375, Mamaearth 400ml ₹374-₹499, Babyhug pH 5.5 400ml ₹835. Baru Sahib winter dryness makes this a near-daily product for babies AND adults — the largest volume line in the toiletries block. Stock the 400ml deep before November.

skuLines.line: Baby cold cream / winter face cream
skuLines.examples: Himalaya Baby Cream 50/100g; Mamaearth Milky Soft Face Cream 60g; Babyhug pH 5.5 Peach Milk Cream; Cetaphil Baby Cream
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Feb — the sharpest single seasonal spike in this whole category at a cold hill location
skuLines.notes: Verified Himalaya Baby Cream from ₹105, Mamaearth 60g ₹175, Babyhug ₹489, Cetaphil ₹621. Chapped cheeks on a Baru Sahib toddler in January is the seasonal certainty to buy against. Order the winter block in September before hill freight gets slow, and expect adult crossover so the volume is bigger than the baby count implies.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Baby Powder 50/100/200/400g; Johnson's Baby Powder; Ponds Dreamflower (crossover); Mee Mee baby powder
skuLines.seasonality: Apr-Sep peak (hot and humid); falls away in winter
skuLines.notes: Verified Himalaya baby powder from ₹57. Cheap, indefinite shelf life, adult crossover to students and staff — a low-risk facing. Modern paediatric advice is moving away from talc on infants, so lead with the rash cream, not the powder, when a mother asks about nappy rash.

skuLines.examples: Nycil Prickly Heat Powder 150g; Himalaya Prickly Heat Baby Powder; Dermi Cool; Boroplus Prickly Heat
skuLines.notes: Verified Nycil 150g ₹139, Himalaya prickly heat baby powder from ₹112. Heavy monsoon at 173101 plus hostel dormitories means this sells to students and staff far beyond the baby cohort — treat it as a seasonal general-store line stocked out of the baby aisle from April, cleared by October. Do not carry winter stock.

skuLines.examples: Mamaearth Milky Soft Mineral Sunscreen SPF 30 PA+++ 80g; Aveeno Baby sunscreen; Sebamed Baby sun lotion
skuLines.notes: Verified Mamaearth 80g ₹283. Newly available as a baby-specific line (last ~2 years). Genuinely relevant at Baru Sahib's altitude where UV is materially higher than the plains, and there is no other source on campus. One SKU, Mar-Sep.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Baby Kajal; Babyhug 100% Natural Kajal 8g; Mee Mee kajal
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; gifting spike at births and festivals
skuLines.notes: Verified Babyhug 8g ₹164-₹245. Culturally standard in North Indian and Punjabi households — an assortment that omits it is a foreign assortment. Tiny, high margin, long shelf life, and a near-certain purchase for every new baby on campus. Stock it beside the massage oil, not the cosmetics.

skuLines.examples: Himalaya Baby Laundry Wash; Mee Mee Baby Laundry Detergent 500ml/1L; Mamaearth Plant Based Baby Laundry Liquid; Puramate
skuLines.seasonality: Year-round; peaks in monsoon when cloth nappy loads double
skuLines.notes: Verified ₹267-₹339 for 500ml-1L, ₹662 for 1L pouch. Two buyers: staff families washing cloth nappies, and the hostel washing bedwetting bedding. Heavy — order with a dry-goods consignment, not with diapers. Refill pouches beat bottles on freight per litre.

skuLines.examples: Mee Mee fluoride-free toothpaste; Chicco baby toothpaste; Himalaya Kids toothpaste; finger brush and silicone first brush
skuLines.notes: Starts at ~6 months with the first tooth, so every infant on campus needs it within a year. Also feeds straight into the pre-primary Academy cohort, which is much larger than the infant cohort — the real volume is 2-6 year olds.

skuLines.examples: Philips Avent Natural 125/260ml; Pigeon Peristaltic Plus 240ml; Mee Mee bottle; LuvLap Anti-Colic; Chicco Well Being
skuLines.marginBand: 25-40% — the best margin in the category
skuLines.notes: Verified Philips Avent 260ml ₹499-₹899, Chicco glass ₹599, Pigeon steel 250ml ₹1,399. 180-270ml is the volume size (694 of 1,372 SKUs); 90-180ml is the newborn size. Look for BPA-free (1,134 SKUs) and anti-colic (835) on the pack — parents read those two words. Under the IMS Act, feeding bottles are also non-promotable: no discounting, no special display.

skuLines.line: Feeding bottle — stainless steel or glass, plus replacement teats
skuLines.examples: Pigeon SoftLatch steel 250ml; Chicco Well Being glass; Avent glass bottle; Pigeon/Avent replacement teats slow-medium-fast flow
skuLines.packSizes: Bottle 240-250ml; teats in packs of 2, flow-graded newborn/slow/medium/fast
skuLines.notes: Steel over glass for this store — glass breaks on hill roads and 221 glass SKUs are not worth the breakage claim. Teats are the repeat-purchase half of the line (replace every 2-3 months) and 205 teat SKUs exist, but they are brand-locked: stock teats ONLY for the bottle brands you actually sell, or you hold dead stock forever.

skuLines.examples: Pigeon/LuvLap bottle and nipple brush set; Chicco bottle cleaning liquid; Milton sterilising tablets; microwave steam sterilising bags; LuvLap electric steam sterilizer
skuLines.packSizes: Brush singles; liquid 400-500ml; tablets 20-30s; steam bags 5-10s; sterilizer 1 unit
skuLines.notes: The brush and liquid are the must-haves — 330 bottle-cleaning SKUs nationally vs only 71 sterilizers. Sterilising tablets are the right hill product: light, cheap, no electricity, no breakage, indefinite shelf life. Carry ONE electric sterilizer as a display/special-order item, not stock — ₹2,000-5,000 of dead capital otherwise.

skuLines.line: Sippers, cups, bowls, spoons and bibs
skuLines.examples: Pigeon spout cup; Mee Mee straw sipper; Chicco suction bowl; Babyhug bowl-and-spoon set; silicone catch bib; cloth bibs pack of 5
skuLines.packSizes: Sipper 150-300ml; bowl+spoon sets; bibs single or 3/5-packs
skuLines.notes: Weaning hardgoods — the 6-12 month attachment sale after formula and cereal. Unbreakable, never expires, best margin per rupee of freight in the whole category. 1,473 sipper and 2,517 bib SKUs exist nationally; carry 3-4 total, chosen on colour appeal not features.

skuLines.line: Breastfeeding support — pump, storage, pads, nipple cream
skuLines.examples: Pigeon manual breast pump; LuvLap manual pump; Mee Mee breast milk storage bottles/bags; disposable nursing pads; lanolin nipple cream
skuLines.packSizes: Pump 1 unit; storage bottles 4-6; bags 25-30s; pads 30-60s; cream 15-30g
skuLines.notes: 1,024 breast-feeding SKUs nationally. This is the mother-side half of the lane and it is where a working teaching mother on campus is most stranded — she cannot drive to town for nursing pads. Nipple cream and pads are the true repeat items; the pump is one-off and should be a special order. Note: the IMS Act's promotion ban does NOT restrict breastfeeding aids, so these you may display and promote freely — and arguably should.

skuLines.examples: Woodward's Gripe Water 130/200ml; Himalaya Bonnisan liquid/drops; Colicaid drops; Dabur Gripe Water
skuLines.notes: Verified Woodward's ~₹79-₹100 for a single bottle, ₹199 for a 2-pack; Bonnisan-class ayurvedic ₹142-₹201. A colicky infant at 2am with no pharmacy for 30-50 km is the single most predictable emergency on this campus. Most of these are Ayurvedic proprietary medicines — confirm whether ARY's licences cover them; the allopathic simethicone drops (Colicaid) may need a pharmacy.

skuLines.line: Baby thermometer, nasal aspirator and saline drops
skuLines.examples: Dr Trust / Omron digital thermometer; infrared forehead thermometer; Pigeon nasal aspirator; Nasoclear / Nasivion Baby saline drops
skuLines.notes: A blocked nose in a Baru Sahib January is the routine reason a household leaves campus. Digital thermometer and saline drops are cheap, unbreakable, never expire, and stop that trip. Saline nasal drops are a drug in India — check whether they need a pharmacy licence before shelving; the aspirator and thermometer are devices and do not.

skuLines.examples: Chicco Physio soother; Pigeon Minimal pacifier; Mee Mee water-filled teether; silicone fruit teether; Babyhug teething ring
skuLines.notes: Verified ₹162-₹219 typical on Amazon. 2,972 SKUs nationally — hopelessly overserved online, so compete on having ONE in stock today rather than on choice. Unbreakable, no expiry, excellent margin, near-zero freight cost. Classic impulse buy at the till of a baby counter.

skuLines.line: Baby nail clipper, grooming kit, brush and comb
skuLines.examples: Babyhug baby nail clipper; Chicco grooming set; Mee Mee soft brush and comb set; rounded-tip baby scissors
skuLines.notes: Verified Babyhug 7-in-1 electric clipper ₹684-₹845; manual clippers ₹149-₹299. Stick to the manual clipper and brush-comb set — the electric one is a gift SKU, not a need. Never expires, ships flat, high margin. The natural anchor of a 'new baby box' bundle.

skuLines.line: Baby mosquito repellent — patches, roll-on, bands
skuLines.examples: Goodknight Patches; Mamaearth Natural Anti-Mosquito Roll-On; Herbal Strategi patches; repellent bands
skuLines.notes: Heavy monsoon at 173101 makes Jul-Sep the window. Baby-safe DEET-free formats only — a plug-in vaporiser is not the same product and parents know it. Cheap, light, high margin, but strictly seasonal: buy in June, clear by October, carry no winter stock.

trends2026: Pant-style has all but replaced taped: 1,351 pant vs 285 taped diaper SKUs on FirstCry (Aug 2026), and taped now survives essentially only in newborn/XS. A 2026 assortment that leads with taped is a 2015 assortment.

HMO-fortified formula is the premium claim of the moment — Similac Plus with 5-HMOs, Nestle NAN Excellapro's DHA/ARA recipe, Aptamil Gold+ — with Mordor Intelligence flagging 2'-FL oligosaccharide fortification as a top India baby-food trend and Milk Formula still holding 44.78% of a USD 10.49 bn (2026) India baby food market.

Organic and chemical-free is the fastest-growing half of the market though still the smaller half: natural/organic baby care is forecast at 13.88% CAGR against synthetic's 77.08% 2025 share (Mordor), and FirstCry now lists 290 organic and 340 'no artificial colour' baby-food SKUs.

'No refined sugar / no preservatives' has become the default claim on mainstream baby cereal, not a differentiator — Nestle's own Cerelac range now leads its pack copy with it across Ragi, Wheat Apple, Khichdi-Vegetables-and-Ghee and Multigrain variants.

Indian traditional weaning grains have become a branded category: ragi (99 SKUs), multigrain (116), sathu maavu (29), millets (32) and sprouted ragi (39) on FirstCry, driven by Timios, Slurrp Farm, ByGrandma, Little Moppet Foods and Tummy Friendly Foods — at 20-35% retailer margin versus 8-14% on Cerelac.

99%-water, unscented and paraben-free wipes are displacing scented: 288 unscented against 375 scented SKUs, 538 paraben-free and 210 '99% water' — and per-wipe pricing (₹0.67 to ₹2.09) is now shown on-shelf and online, which makes the category directly comparable for the first time.

Reusable cloth diapering has turned into a real D2C segment (SuperBottoms, Bumtum, Bummy Pants, Allter, 4,019 cloth SKUs) and non-disposables are the fastest-growing diaper sub-segment at roughly 7.8% CAGR off an 8.4% base — genuinely rational for a hill campus with water and labour on site.

pH 5.5 / dermatologist-tested 'sensitive' sub-ranges have moved down from pharmacy brands into mass: Himalaya Sensitive, Babyhug Pro Sensitive pH 5.5, Sebamed — parents now read pH off the pack the way they read SPF.

Ready-to-feed purees and pouches are India's fastest-growing baby food format at 7.98% CAGR (Mordor), and baby mineral sunscreen (Mamaearth SPF 30 PA+++, 80g, ₹283) has appeared as a new baby-specific line in the last two years.

Channel shift is real but supermarkets still win: 36.37% of India baby care went through supermarkets/hypermarkets in 2025 against online's fastest 12.57% CAGR — which for a captive township means a physical counter still holds the category if it simply does not go out of stock.
adjacentServices: Birth-month register and automatic stage-progression: in a closed township you can log every infant's birth month once, then have Stage 2 formula and the next diaper size land before the household runs out. No open retailer can do this, and it is the single highest-value service in this category.

Standing monthly order for staff-quarter families — one reserved monthly diaper pack and one formula tin per named household. Solves both sides at once: the family never stocks out, and ARY does not carry ₹3,000 monthly packs speculatively.
Free baby weigh-in and a growth chart at the counter. Costs one ₹2,000 scale, brings the mother back every month, and tells you her baby's diaper size before she does.
WhatsApp reorder plus delivery to staff quarters — a mother with a colicky newborn will not walk to the store at 9pm, and this is exactly when rash cream and gripe water are needed.

Bulk indent line for the Academy infirmary, creche and hostel matrons: bedwetting pull-ups, bed protectors, baby laundry liquid, thermometers, cotton wool. An institutional buyer, invoiced monthly, that no consumer shelf reaches.

New-baby starter box for staff families: cloth nappies, langot, massage oil, kajal, rash cream, soap, towel, nail clipper. A one-time curated bundle at 30-40% blended margin that lands the household as a repeat customer for the next three years.

Second-hand board for outgrown hardgoods — bottles, sterilizers, cloth diapers, bathtubs. Only works in a closed community where both parties are known, and it earns goodwill on items ARY makes no margin holding.

Short-date clearance shelf for purees, snacks and cereal, published monthly. CAUTION: this must exclude infant formula and infant foods for under-2s — the IMS Act 1992 bars discounts, coupons and special displays on those, so mark them down at your legal peril.

Cloth-nappy laundry tie-in with the campus laundry, sold as a monthly service alongside the reusable-diaper sale. Turns a one-off ₹1,000 purchase into recurring revenue and removes the one real objection (nothing dries in monsoon).

Regulatory constraints stated from domain knowledge, NOT verified live this session (indiacode.nic.in and bpni.org both returned 403/404): the Infant Milk Substitutes, Feeding Bottles and Infant Foods Act 1992 (amended 2003) and FSSAI licensing for infant food. Treat the IMS Act specifics as ~85% confidence and confirm the current text before writing shelf or pricing policy on formula, infant foods for under-2s, and feeding bottles.

GST rates deliberately omitted per line: the Sept-2025 rate rationalisation moved several baby items (diapers, infant milk food, toiletries) and I could not verify the current slab for each HSN this session. Confirm off a live purchase invoice before using any rate in a margin calculation.
